prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision: A fairer, greener UK that tackles the cost-of-living, rebuilds public services, and responds to the climate and nature emergencies with urgency, social justice and hope.

Health and care
- NHS: Reverse underfunding and privatisation; faster GP access, guaranteed NHS dentistry, fair pay (including junior doctors), major capital repair/build. Extra revenue spend rising to c. £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years.
- Primary care/public health: More GP funding, cut admin, expand community diagnostics; restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn).
- Dentistry: New NHS contract; investment reaching £3bn/yr by 2030.
- Mental health: 28‑day access to evidence-based therapies; counsellor in every school and sixth‑form; tailored services.
- Social care: Free personal care; national career/pay structure; £20bn/yr; protections for unpaid and migrant carers.

Homes and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/yr; end Right to Buy; bring empty homes into use.
- Renters: Local rent controls; end Section 21; new long-term tenancies; tenant right to energy upgrades.
- Retrofit: Five‑year £29bn for home insulation (to EPC B), £9bn for heat pumps, £7bn for summer heat adaptation; area‑based programmes; higher standards for new builds (Passivhaus-equivalent, solar, heat pumps).
- Planning: Protect Green Belt; nature-positive, low-car developments; whole-life carbon rules.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax rising over a decade; phase out nuclear; expand grid, storage, interconnectors.
- Renewables: Wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets by 2035 of 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; remove barriers to community energy; public ownership of Crown Estate’s energy assets.
- Just transition: Skills/training £4bn/yr; Offshore Energy and Skills Passport; minimum community ownership in local projects.

Economy and tax
- Green investment: Average £40bn/yr for clean power, housing retrofit, rail/electrification, active travel, industry decarbonisation, water/sewage.
- Public ownership: Rail, water, and Big 5 retail energy back in public hands.
- Fair taxes: Wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NIC upper limit; fairer inheritance; stronger anti‑avoidance; higher windfall taxes.
- Carbon tax: Initially ~£120/t, rising towards £500/t within 10 years.

Work, welfare and equality
- Workers’ rights: Repeal anti‑union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage for all ages; 10:1 pay ratio cap; full rights from day one; protect gig workers; move towards a 4‑day week.
- Social security: +£40/wk to UC and legacy benefits; abolish two‑child cap and five‑week wait; +5% disability benefits; keep triple lock; raise carers allowance; scrap bedroom tax; end sanctions; long‑term Universal Basic Income.

Nature, food and animals
- Rights of Nature Act; 30% of land/sea for nature by 2030; re‑nationalise water; Clean Air Act; +£1.5bn for DEFRA and regulators; restore rivers/peat/woodland.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support for nature‑friendly, mixed and horticultural production; cut pesticides; fair supply chains; free school meals for all and breakfast to Year 6.
- Animal welfare: Ban blood sports, factory farming practices, lead ammo, destructive fishing in MPAs; establish Commission on Animal Protection.

Education
- End tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; invest £8bn in schools (+£2.5bn/yr for repairs/RAAC); £5bn for SEND; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; 35 hours/week childcare from 9 months; £1.4bn for Sure Start; boost FE/sixth‑form and lifelong learning.

Transport
- Shift from roads to public/active travel: Free buses for under‑18s; higher bus/rail subsidies (to £10bn/yr); £19bn over five years for public transport and active travel; public rail; £2.5bn/yr for cycle/walking; oppose new roads; EV scrappage rising to £5bn/yr; end new petrol/diesel sales by 2027; default 20mph in built‑up areas; frequent‑flyer levy; no domestic flights under 3‑hour rail.

Democracy, rights, migration, culture, justice
- Democracy: Proportional representation; replace Lords with elected chamber; votes at 16; repeal Elections Act; fair party funding; stronger lobbying transparency; protect HRA/ECHR; self‑ID for trans people.
- Migration: End hostile environment/NRPF/10‑year route; safe asylum routes; right to work while awaiting decisions; new Department of Migration.
- Culture/media/digital: £5bn for community arts/sport; cap media ownership at 20%; implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; robust, rights‑based AI regulation.
- Policing/justice: Community policing; end routine stop‑and‑search/facial recognition; presumption against <2‑year prison terms; decriminalise personal drug possession; £11bn to fix courts/legal aid; tackle VAWG; decriminalise sex work.

Foreign policy
- Support Ukraine; pursue EU rejoin (customs union first, restore free movement/Erasmus); Gaza/Israel: immediate bilateral ceasefire, recognise Palestine, end UK arms exports to Israel, back war crimes investigations.
- Nuclear/NATO: Sign TPNW, cancel Trident; push NATO reforms (No First Use, diplomacy-first).
- Aid/climate finance: Restore aid to 0.7% GNI then 1% by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI; support Loss & Damage; back anti‑ecocide law; fair trade without corporate courts.
